title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 1
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 1

THE TWELVE SOVEREIGNS OF ETERNITA
subtitle: The Twelve Dragons Who Shaped Serantia
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
Before the first kingdom raised its banners, before the first mortal drew breath, and before the first star illuminated the heavens, the Twelve Sovereigns stood beside the First Dragon and gave shape to existence.

Each was entrusted with one of the twelve great influences that govern Serantia. None was created to rule alone, for each represented a necessary truth of creation. Water could not exist without a world to contain it. Fire could not burn without something to consume. Life could not flourish without death, and light could hold no meaning without darkness.

Together, the Twelve forged the world and populated it with creatures bearing the essence of their respective influences. Though the First Dragon stood above them all, the Council of Eternita was the instrument through which his vision became reality.

These are their names, their legacies, and the powers they bestowed upon Serantia.

I. LINDWORM

The Dragon of None | Sovereign of the Unbound | Keeper of the First Form

The Lindworm was the first of the Twelve to understand that creation required more than extraordinary power. It required simplicity.

While its brethren shaped the fundamental forces of existence, the Lindworm was entrusted with that which belonged to none of them: the ordinary, the unaligned, and the creatures whose existence required no extraordinary explanation.

It shaped the first beasts to walk upon the earth, the birds that filled the skies, and the creatures that swam through rivers and streams. It gave the world its deer and wolves, its rabbits and bears, its cattle and horses. These were not creatures of elemental fury or magical wonder. They were the foundation upon which the diversity of life could flourish.

Yet the Lindworm’s dominion extended beyond the mundane.

It represented the freedom of existence itself: the right of a thing to be what it was, without the influence of a greater power defining its nature. Where other dragons imposed their essence upon their creations, the Lindworm allowed its creatures to develop through instinct, adaptation, and the demands of survival.

It was the guardian of possibility in its purest form.

The Lindworm is often depicted as a long-bodied dragon of ancient design, possessing powerful limbs, a serpentine form, and scales that bear no fixed elemental coloration. Its appearance changes across the oldest depictions, as though no single form could fully capture its nature.

Among the Council, the Lindworm is considered quiet and contemplative. It rarely seeks recognition, for it understands that the greatest contributions to a world are not always the most spectacular.

Its Legacy: The Lindworm gave Serantia its ordinary creatures and established the principle that no being must be extraordinary to possess value. Its influence can be found wherever life survives through its own strength rather than the intervention of greater powers.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 2
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 2

II. Y DDRAIG GOCH
subtitle: The Dragon of Fire | Sovereign of the Inferno | The Crimson Devourer
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
When the First Dragon commanded that the world be given warmth, the Y Ddraig Goch opened its jaws and breathed the first flame into existence.

It was not a mere fire that emerged, but the primordial principle of combustion itself: the power to transform one thing into another through destruction. From that first breath came the molten heart of Serantia, the world’s volcanoes, and the fires that would one day warm mortal hearths and illuminate the darkness.

The Y Ddraig Goch is a dragon of terrible majesty, bearing crimson scales that glow like heated iron and horns that resemble the jagged peaks of a volcanic range. Its wings stretch across the heavens like banners of war, and its breath can turn stone to rivers of molten earth.

Yet the Y Ddraig Goch is not simply the embodiment of destruction.

Fire consumes, but it also purifies. It destroys the old so that the new may emerge. It hardens metal, prepares the soil for renewal, and gives warmth to life that would otherwise perish beneath the cold. The Dragon of Fire understands this balance better than any of its brethren.

Its temper is fierce, its pride immense, and its judgment swift. It believes that weakness must be challenged and that stagnation is a fate worse than destruction. To the Y Ddraig Goch, the greatest tragedy is not to be defeated, but to refuse to rise again.

Among the Twelve, it is one of the most formidable in direct combat, and its wrath has become the subject of countless legends. Nevertheless, it bows to the First Dragon, recognizing that even the fiercest flame must have a purpose beyond itself.

Its Legacy: The Y Ddraig Goch gave Serantia fire, heat, volcanic power, and the transformative force of destruction and rebirth. Every flame, from the smallest candle to the eruption of a mighty volcano, carries a fragment of its primordial gift.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 3
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 3

III. HRIMWYRM
subtitle: The Dragon of Frost | Sovereign of Winter | Keeper of the Eternal Stillness
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
Where the Y Ddraig Goch brought forth flame, the Hrimwyrm brought forth the cold.

Its breath swept across the highest peaks of Serantia, coating their summits in ice and transforming the barren reaches of the world into vast frozen kingdoms. Glaciers emerged in its wake, snow began to fall from the heavens, and the first winters settled upon the land.

The Hrimwyrm is a colossal dragon of pale blue, white, and crystalline silver, with horns like branching ice formations and scales that shimmer as though carved from ancient glaciers. Its wings are broad and angular, and the air around its body grows still as warmth drains from the world.

The Hrimwyrm is patient beyond measure. It does not rush, does not boast, and does not expend its strength without purpose. It understands that time can accomplish what force cannot, that even the mightiest mountain may be slowly carved by ice, and that endurance is often more powerful than fury.

Frost is not merely cold. It is preservation, silence, and the suspension of change. Under its influence, things may endure long after they should have perished. Ancient secrets remain buried beneath glaciers, forgotten creatures sleep within frozen caverns, and relics of ages past survive untouched by the passage of time.

Yet the Hrimwyrm also understands that stillness cannot last forever. Winter must eventually yield, and the ice must one day melt. Its dominion is not the permanent denial of life, but the recognition that every living thing requires moments of rest, retreat, and preservation.

It is among the most reserved members of the Council, speaking rarely but with a gravity that commands attention.

Its Legacy: The Hrimwyrm gave Serantia ice, snow, glaciers, and the power of preservation. Its influence endures in the frozen wastes, the creatures of winter, and the ancient things that remain hidden beneath the ice.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 4
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 4

IV. PIASA
subtitle: The Dragon of Storm | Sovereign of the Tempest | The Thunder Above the World
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
Before the first storm crossed the heavens, the sky was silent.

Then Piasa spread its wings.

Thunder shattered the silence, lightning split the clouds, and winds swept across the newborn world. The heavens were no longer an empty expanse above the earth, but a living domain of motion, fury, and untamed power.

Piasa is a magnificent and terrifying dragon, its body bearing the features of a celestial predator. Its immense wings command the winds, its talons crackle with lightning, and its eyes burn with the brilliance of a storm about to break. Its appearance is often described as a fusion of dragon, bird, and ancient sky-beast, reflecting its dominion over all that moves through the air.

Of the Twelve, Piasa is among the most restless. It despises stagnation and views movement as the natural state of existence. Winds must blow, clouds must travel, and the heavens must remain free. To imprison the sky would be to deny the world one of its most fundamental freedoms.

Piasa’s power is not confined to destruction. Storms bring rain to parched lands, carry seeds across distant territories, and replenish the rivers upon which life depends. Lightning can destroy a forest, but it can also ignite the changes through which new growth emerges.

The Dragon of Storm is proud, unpredictable, and difficult to command. It often challenges the judgments of its brethren, not from malice, but because it believes that even the wisest authority must be tested.

Yet Piasa is fiercely loyal to the First Dragon. It remembers that the sky was once nothing more than emptiness, and that it was granted the freedom to fill that emptiness with motion.

Its Legacy: Piasa gave Serantia the winds, lightning, thunder, and the great storms that sweep across its lands and seas. Every tempest that shakes the world echoes the first beating of its wings.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 5
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 5

V. FAFNIR
subtitle: The Dragon of Earth | Sovereign of Stone | The Foundation of the World
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
When the First Dragon commanded that Serantia be given a foundation, Fafnir descended into the formless depths and began to shape the bones of the world.

It raised mountains from the darkness, carved vast caverns through the stone, and laid the mineral veins that would one day sustain civilizations. It created the cliffs that defied the sea, the valleys that sheltered life, and the bedrock upon which every kingdom would eventually stand.

Fafnir is a mighty dragon of immense proportions, armored in scales resembling black iron, weathered granite, and precious mineral deposits. Crystalline formations crown its head, while its claws can split the earth and reshape the landscape with every movement.

It is the most steadfast of the Twelve, possessing a will that is nearly impossible to bend. Fafnir believes that everything worth preserving must possess a strong foundation. A kingdom built upon ambition alone will crumble. A promise unsupported by action is meaningless. Even the greatest creation is doomed if its foundations are weak.

Earth represents more than physical strength. It is permanence, possession, and the weight of consequence. Mountains endure long after their creators have passed, and the treasures buried within them may outlast entire civilizations.

Fafnir understands the danger of this permanence. The earth can shelter, but it can also imprison. Wealth can sustain, but it can also corrupt. Strength can protect, but it can also become tyranny.

These truths have made Fafnir cautious in its judgments and difficult to sway. It does not act quickly, but once it has committed itself to a cause, few forces in Serantia can move it from its chosen path.

Its Legacy: Fafnir gave Serantia its mountains, caverns, metals, minerals, and the strength of the earth. Every fortress raised upon stone and every treasure hidden beneath the ground bears witness to its work.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 6
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 6

VI. GARGOUILLE
subtitle: The Dragon of Water | Sovereign of the Deep | Keeper of the Endless Cycle
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
When the world had been raised from the void, Gargouille filled its hollows with water.

Oceans spread across the newborn earth, rivers carved their paths through the mountains, and rain descended from the heavens. The world received its first great cycle: water rising, falling, flowing, and returning, forever moving yet never truly lost.

Gargouille is a formidable aquatic dragon whose scales resemble deep sapphire, polished silver, and the shifting colors of the sea. Its body is long and powerful, adapted to the crushing depths of the oceans, while its great jaws and horns evoke the ancient terrors of the waters. Its presence can summon waves that tower over coastlines or still the surface of an entire sea.

Gargouille is among the most adaptable of the Twelve. It understands that survival often requires transformation, and that the strongest are not always those who resist change, but those who learn to endure it.

Water can be gentle enough to sustain the smallest creature, yet powerful enough to swallow entire cities. It can preserve life, erode mountains, conceal treasures, and carry the remnants of fallen kingdoms into the deepest reaches of the sea.

For Gargouille, these are not contradictions. They are the nature of existence.

Its temperament is calm, observant, and difficult to provoke. Like the ocean, it can remain peaceful for ages before revealing a fury that no mortal force can withstand. It respects patience and wisdom, believing that the world belongs not to those who demand the most from it, but to those who understand its rhythms.

Of all the Twelve, Gargouille may possess the greatest awareness of the world’s hidden history. The waters remember what the land forgets, and the depths preserve secrets that no civilization was ever meant to uncover.

Its Legacy: Gargouille gave Serantia its oceans, rivers, lakes, rain, and the creatures of the deep. Every current and tide reflects its eternal work, carrying life and memory across the world.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 7
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 7

VII. MOKELE-MBEMBE
subtitle: The Dragon of Nature | Sovereign of the Wild | The First Breath of Life
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
When the earth had been shaped and the waters had begun to flow, Mokele-mbembe brought forth the living world.

It spread forests across the continents, covered barren lands in grass, and filled the valleys with plants and trees. It awakened the instincts of beasts and established the great cycles of growth, hunger, reproduction, and decay.

Mokele-mbembe is an immense dragon whose form evokes the ancient creatures of primordial wilderness. Its long neck rises above the canopy of the world’s oldest forests, its body is covered in verdant scales and moss-like growths, and its great limbs possess the strength to uproot trees and reshape the landscape. Vines and flowering plants cling to its hide, while its passing leaves behind fertile soil and flourishing vegetation.

It is the most deeply connected to the living world of all the Twelve.

To Mokele-mbembe, nature is neither kind nor cruel. It simply is. The predator must hunt, the prey must flee, the forest must grow, and the old must eventually give way to the new. Every death nourishes another life, and every ending becomes the foundation of something yet to come.

It despises those who seek to dominate life without understanding it. Yet it does not condemn civilization merely for existing. It recognizes that mortals, too, are creatures of the world and that their greatest achievements can coexist with the wilderness when built upon understanding rather than greed.

Mokele-mbembe is patient with the young, protective of its creations, and merciless toward those who threaten the balance of life. It does not seek to freeze the world in its original state, for nature must change to remain alive.

Among the Council, it is perhaps the greatest reminder that creation was never intended to be static.

Its Legacy: Mokele-mbembe gave Serantia its forests, flora, ecosystems, and the countless creatures that inhabit its wild places. Every seed that takes root and every beast that survives the wilderness carries its influence.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 8
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 8

VIII. OUROBOROS
subtitle: The Dragon of Void | Sovereign of the Abyss | The End That Precedes the Beginning
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
Before Serantia could exist, there had to be a place for it to exist within.

That place belonged to Ouroboros.

While the other dragons shaped the substance of creation, Ouroboros shaped the spaces between things. It established the boundaries between existence and nonexistence, opened the vast distances beyond the stars, and gave form to the empty expanse from which the world had emerged.

Ouroboros is a strange and terrible dragon, often depicted as a colossal serpent curled into a circle, its tail resting within its own jaws. Its scales resemble the starless depths of space, and its body seems to vanish into itself, as though it occupies a place beyond ordinary dimensions.

Its nature is difficult for even the other Sovereigns to comprehend.

Void is not simply darkness, for Darkness has its own sovereign. Nor is it destruction, for destruction requires something that can be destroyed. Void is absence itself: the space left behind when something is removed, the silence beyond sound, and the possibility that remains when all known things have vanished.

Ouroboros understands that creation cannot expand without boundaries to cross, nor can existence possess meaning without the possibility of nonexistence. It is the keeper of the world’s edges and the guardian of the spaces where the laws of Serantia begin to weaken.

It is neither benevolent nor malicious. It observes, endures, and accepts the possibility of endings that its brethren would rather deny.

Its name reflects the most unsettling truth of its nature: the end and the beginning are not always separate things. What disappears may return in another form, and what seems eternal may one day consume itself.

Of all the Twelve, Ouroboros may be the most difficult to predict, for its understanding of existence extends beyond the boundaries by which the others define themselves.

Its Legacy: Ouroboros gave Serantia the Void, the spaces beyond creation, and the boundaries separating the known world from the unknown. Its influence is felt wherever reality thins and the impossible threatens to enter.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 9
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 9

IX. FAIRY DRAGON
subtitle: The Dragon of Fae | Sovereign of Wonder | Keeper of the Impossible
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
When the world had been given form, life, and the laws by which it would function, the Fairy Dragon asked a question that none of its brethren had considered.

What if the world could be otherwise?

And so it brought wonder into existence.

The Fairy Dragon created the strange paths that led nowhere and everywhere, the enchanted groves where time flowed differently, and the hidden realms where mortal understanding held no authority. It filled Serantia with illusion, enchantment, dreams, and the capricious magic of the Fae.

The Fairy Dragon is unlike the other Sovereigns in appearance. It is often described as an elegant, iridescent dragon whose scales shimmer with shifting colors, whose wings resemble delicate panes of living light, and whose horns and tail are adorned with strange natural ornaments. Though smaller in many depictions than its colossal brethren, its true size is said to depend upon the perspective of the observer.

Its power does not rely upon brute force. It thrives upon possibility, imagination, and the willingness to believe that reality is not as fixed as it appears.

The Fairy Dragon is playful, curious, and endlessly inventive. Yet its whimsy conceals a dangerous nature. Fae magic does not necessarily obey mortal ideas of fairness, and the Fairy Dragon understands that wonder can inspire both delight and terror.

A gift may become a curse. A promise may bind its recipient for centuries. A beautiful garden may conceal a realm from which no traveler can return.

To the Fairy Dragon, these are not cruelties but reminders that the unknown must be approached with humility.

It is deeply protective of its creations, especially those that exist beyond the understanding of the other Sovereigns. It believes that a world stripped of mystery would be a world stripped of one of its greatest treasures.

Its Legacy: The Fairy Dragon gave Serantia its Fae realms, enchantments, illusions, and impossible wonders. Every enchanted forest, strange bargain, and dream that seems more real than waking life bears the mark of its influence.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 10
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 10

X. AZI DAHAKA
subtitle: The Dragon of Darkness | Sovereign of Shadows | Keeper of the Unseen
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
When Radiance illuminated the heavens, Azi Dahaka drew forth the shadows.

It spread night across the world, creating the darkness beneath the forests, the depths of caverns, and the great hours of stillness when the world could rest. It established the veil between what could be seen and what remained hidden.

Azi Dahaka is a dreadful dragon of blackened scales, obsidian horns, and immense wings that swallow the light around them. Its eyes gleam from within a face of ancient menace, and its long body seems to blend into the darkness even when standing beneath the open sky.

Yet Azi Dahaka is not the embodiment of evil.

Darkness is the refuge of the weary, the shelter of the hunted, and the veil beneath which countless creatures survive. It is the secret that protects the innocent, the silence that allows thought, and the night that makes the stars visible.

Azi Dahaka understands these truths, but it also understands darkness’s more terrible possibilities. Fear can be a weapon. Secrets can corrupt. Hidden ambitions can grow unchecked when no one dares to expose them.

The Dragon of Darkness is calculating, proud, and fiercely independent. It believes that truth is not always virtuous simply because it is revealed, and that some knowledge must remain concealed for the sake of the world. It rarely offers explanations, preferring to allow others to discover the consequences of their own assumptions.

This has earned it the distrust of several of its brethren, particularly Radiance. Yet the two are bound by an ancient understanding: neither can fulfill its purpose without the other.

For a world of eternal light would be as incomplete as a world of eternal night.

Its Legacy: Azi Dahaka gave Serantia darkness, night, shadows, and the unseen places of the world. Every nocturnal creature and every secret preserved beneath the veil of darkness carries a fragment of its gift.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 11
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 11

XI. LADON
subtitle: The Dragon of Arcane | Sovereign of Mysteries | Architect of Magic
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
When Serantia had been given substance, Ladon established the principles through which that substance could be changed.

It wove the unseen currents of magic through the world, established the fundamental laws governing supernatural power, and created the means by which knowledge could be transformed into action. It gave existence its hidden architecture, allowing the impossible to become possible through understanding.

Ladon is a magnificent dragon adorned with intricate scales that resemble enchanted metal and polished gemstones. Runes of ancient power trace their way across its body, shifting and rearranging themselves according to mysteries beyond mortal comprehension. Its horns form elaborate spirals, and its eyes burn with the brilliance of a mind that has spent ages studying the secrets of creation.

Of the Twelve, Ladon is the greatest scholar of existence.

It seeks to understand everything: the laws of nature, the structure of the Void, the strange logic of the Fae, and the relationship between the elemental forces. Where its brethren accept certain mysteries as fundamental truths, Ladon asks why those truths exist and whether they might be altered.

Arcane power is not inherently benevolent or destructive. It is a tool, and its consequences depend upon the knowledge, intent, and discipline of those who wield it.

This belief makes Ladon a tireless teacher, but also a dangerous experimenter. It has pursued questions that others consider forbidden, not out of malice, but because it believes ignorance is a greater threat than knowledge.

Ladon respects the First Dragon above all others, for it recognizes that the creation of Serantia represents the greatest act of applied power ever performed. Yet it also understands that the First Dragon’s work may contain secrets even the creator himself has not fully explored.

Among the Council, Ladon is often the one called upon when the laws of reality are challenged or when a mystery threatens to destabilize the world.

Its Legacy: Ladon gave Serantia its arcane laws, magical currents, and the principles that allow spellcraft and supernatural knowledge to function. Every spell, enchantment, and magical discovery is made possible by the foundations it established.

title: Tome of the Dragons, V. 12
heading:
TOME OF THE DRAGONS
V. 12

XII. SERAPHIM
subtitle: The Dragon of Radiance | Sovereign of the Dawn | Bearer of the First Light
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
When Serantia had been shaped and its mysteries established, Seraphim brought light into the heavens.

It ignited the brilliance of the stars, illuminated the newborn world, and established the great contrast between revelation and concealment. Through its power, the world could be seen, understood, and admired in all its splendor.

Seraphim is a majestic dragon whose scales shine with gold, ivory, and celestial silver. Its wings radiate an almost blinding brilliance, and its horns resemble a crown of living sunlight. Its presence can illuminate entire landscapes, while its breath unleashes concentrated radiance capable of piercing the strongest defenses.

Yet Seraphim’s dominion extends beyond physical light.

Radiance represents revelation, clarity, inspiration, and the pursuit of truth. It is the power that exposes corruption, reveals hidden paths, and gives hope to those who believe themselves lost. It can illuminate the world without changing its nature, allowing others to see what was already there.

But Seraphim understands that light can also become a weapon.

Truth can be used to humiliate. Revelation can destroy what was once protected. Those who believe themselves enlightened may become convinced that their judgments are infallible. A light that refuses to acknowledge its own limitations can become as oppressive as the darkness it seeks to banish.

For this reason, Seraphim strives to temper its certainty with wisdom. It believes that truth must be pursued, but that understanding requires more than the ability to see.

Of all the Twelve, Seraphim is among the most closely associated with hope and the preservation of life. Yet it is no gentle guardian when confronted with a force that threatens the existence of Serantia itself.

When it chooses to unleash its full power, even the heavens seem to bend before its radiance.

Its Legacy: Seraphim gave Serantia celestial light, the brilliance of the stars, and the power of revelation. Every dawn, every ray that breaks through the darkness, and every truth brought into the open reflects its eternal influence.

title: Eternita Calling, V. 1
heading:
ETERNITA CALLING
V. 1

THE COUNCIL OF ETERNITA
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
Before Serantia had a name, before its mountains rose and its oceans stirred, there was the First Dragon. From its power and will, existence took shape, and the world was born.

Yet the First Dragon did not shape Serantia alone. Twelve great dragons emerged to govern the forces that would define creation: Lindworm of None, Y Ddraig Goch of Fire, Hrimwyrm of Frost, Piasa of Storm, Fafnir of Earth, Gargouille of Water, Mokele-mbembe of Nature, Ouroboros of Void, the Fairy Dragon of Fae, Azi Dahaka of Darkness, Ladon of Arcane, and Seraphim of Radiance.

Together, these twelve became the Council of Eternita, entrusted with maintaining the balance of the world and guiding the countless creatures born of their influences. Each held dominion over a fundamental aspect of existence, and each understood creation through a different truth. Fire demanded transformation, Frost sought preservation, Nature encouraged growth, and Void reminded all things that even existence had boundaries.

Though their powers differed, their duty remained the same: to protect Serantia and preserve the balance upon which it depended. Yet even among the Council, disagreement endured. What one dragon saw as necessary change, another considered a threat. What one sought to preserve, another believed had already outlived its purpose.

The Council ruled beneath the First Dragon, whose power surpassed them all. They were its stewards, not its equals, charged with guiding the world through the ages while awaiting the return of their creator.

For Serantia was never meant to remain unchanged. It was a living creation, shaped by forces that could nurture, destroy, and begin anew. And the Council would one day learn that preserving the world and preserving its every flaw were not the same thing.

title: Eternita Calling, V. 2
heading:
ETERNITA CALLING
V. 2

THE ETERNITA SLEEP
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
The First Dragon does not rule without end. Bound to a cycle older than the kingdoms of Serantia, it passes through alternating ages of slumber and awakening, each lasting one thousand years.

For one thousand years, the First Dragon sleeps. During this time, the Council of Eternita governs in its stead, maintaining the balance of the world and guiding its many civilizations through prosperity, conflict, and change. Though the First Dragon remains beyond the reach of ordinary affairs, its presence lingers over creation, a silent foundation upon which all existence rests.

Then, after a millennium of slumber, the First Dragon awakens. For the next thousand years, it returns to oversee the world it created, observing the work of the Council and intervening when it deems necessary. Its awakening is a reminder that Serantia belongs to something greater than any kingdom, ruler, or age.

When those thousand years end, the First Dragon returns to sleep, and the cycle begins once more.

This rhythm has endured for ages, becoming the measure by which the oldest traditions mark the passage of time. Yet the Eternita Sleep is more than rest. Each slumber brings renewal, and with renewal comes the shedding of the First Dragon’s ancient skin—a necessary part of its endless cycle.

For countless ages, this shedding was unremarkable. The old skin was discarded, the First Dragon continued its sleep, and Serantia endured.

Until the day the discarded skin refused to remain lifeless.

title: Eternita Calling, V. 3
heading:
ETERNITA CALLING
V. 3

THE SHEDDING
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
Whenever the First Dragon enters its thousand-year slumber, its ancient body undergoes a profound renewal. Its skin, bearing the remnants of ages past, separates from its living form and is left behind as a husk of what once was. The First Dragon emerges renewed, while the discarded skin becomes nothing more than a relic of an earlier age.

This had always been the way of things. The shedding was neither feared nor questioned. It was simply part of the First Dragon’s nature—a reminder that even the mightiest of beings must leave the past behind to continue.

But on one occasion, the discarded skin did not remain lifeless.

Something stirred within the ancient husk. The remnants of the First Dragon’s power gathered, and what should have been nothing more than an empty shell rose into life. It was neither the First Dragon reborn nor one of the twelve Council dragons. It was something unprecedented: a living remnant of the creator, carrying its power without its purpose.

The Council could not agree on what had emerged. Some saw a corruption of the natural order, while others feared it was a consequence of creation that even the First Dragon had never intended. Whatever the truth, the being could not be dismissed as a mere monster. It had come from the very substance of the world’s creator.

It was given two names: the King of Chaos, for the destruction it would bring, and the Last Dragon, for it was believed that no dragon like it would ever exist again.

The event changed the meaning of the shedding forever. What had once symbolized renewal now carried a terrible question: if the First Dragon could cast away its old skin and emerge anew, could Serantia itself do the same?

The Council feared the answer. The Last Dragon embraced it.

title: Eternita Calling, V. 4
heading:
ETERNITA CALLING
V. 4

THE LAST DRAGON
author: Krea, the All Seeing
text:
Born from the discarded skin of the First Dragon, the Last Dragon is a being unlike any other in Serantia. It possesses the power and legacy of its creator, yet it was never granted a place among the Council of Eternita. To the world, it is the King of Chaos—a harbinger of ruin whose arrival threatens everything the Council has sworn to protect.

But the Last Dragon does not believe itself to be evil. It sees Serantia as a world trapped beneath the weight of its own history, its kingdoms repeating old mistakes and its guardians mistaking stagnation for peace. The Council seeks to preserve what exists, even when that existence has become flawed. The Last Dragon sees this as a betrayal of creation’s true nature.

After all, the First Dragon sheds its skin to be renewed. Why, then, should the world be denied the same chance?

The Last Dragon’s purpose is to bring chaos and destruction to Serantia—not simply to end the world, but to force it to change. It seeks to break the structures that have endured for too long, shatter the foundations of stagnant civilizations, and strip the world down until something new can rise from the remnants.

To the Last Dragon, destruction is not the opposite of creation. It is the price creation must sometimes pay to begin again.

Yet its vision carries a terrible danger. A world cannot choose what survives its own destruction, and the Last Dragon cannot promise that Serantia will emerge from the chaos it intends to unleash. It may be seeking renewal, but its methods could leave nothing behind to renew.

The Council calls it a monster. The Last Dragon calls the Council cowards, clinging to an imperfect world because they fear what might come after it. Between them stands Serantia, caught between preservation and transformation, between the familiar world and the terrifying possibility of rebirth.

And so the question remains: when a world becomes imperfect, is it the duty of its guardians to preserve it—or must creation itself be allowed to begin again?
